panel_patterns.interpretation: Mild dyslipidemia with borderline high total cholesterol and triglycerides, LDL‑C near‑optimal. Lifestyle modification is indicated.
Low bicarbonate with rising chloride points to a non‑anion‑gap metabolic acidosis; calcium is low‑normal and glucose is borderline low, supporting a mild metabolic disturbance.

trending_concerns: Urea nitrogen rising from 9.2 to 16.2 mg/dL
overall_assessment: The most urgent issues are a developing non‑anion‑gap metabolic acidosis (low CO₂, high Cl⁻) and a modestly elevated platelet distribution width suggesting platelet activation. Borderline low calcium and glucose, pre‑diabetes (A1c 6.3%) and early dyslipidemia (total cholesterol 185.6 mg/dL, triglycerides 146.1 mg/dL) also merit attention. No critical values are present, but the rising BUN warrants monitoring of renal function.
